summary: Frederick M. Asher worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as a Professor at the University of Minnesota from circa 1974 until 2021.

Frederick M. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held positions at the University of Iowa, where he was attested as a Professor from 2006 to 2008 and as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Frederick Price was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Melbourne and served as Chief Secretary to the Government of Madras in the Madras Civil Service from 1862 to 1897.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell at Cambridge. He was Chief Librarian at the India Office (1903–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937), among other academic appointments.

Frederick Zeuner was a historian and archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Breslau. He later joined the University of London, serving as Lecturer in Geochronology (1936) and Professor of Environmental Archaeology (1946), affiliated with the UCL Institute of Archaeology.

Frederik David Kan Bosch was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden. He directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at Bergen (1961–1972), Oslo (1974), Emory (1989–1996), Harvard (circa 1989–1996), and Boston University (circa 1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri works in sinology and religious studies. She studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer, at Nanjing University, and received her PhD from Heidelberg University (2002). Her academic posts include visiting professorships and research roles at Berlin and Leipzig.

Friedhelm Hardy specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at Münster, Heidelberg, and Oxford under scholars including Paul Hacker, Thomas Burrow, and Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at King's College London (circa 1975–2004).

Friedrich Adolf Krummacher was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1785 to 1789. He held a post at the University of Duisburg from circa 1800 to 1807.

Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and August Boeckh, and later held a post at Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1833 to 1872.

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff worked in sinology, tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning PhDs at Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1964–1982) and the University of Hamburg (1982–1993).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Berlin. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages (1828–1831) and Professor of Sanskrit (1834) at the University of London.

Friedrich August Wilhelm Krahmer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Göttingen (circa 1831–1833). He served as Privatdozent of Oriental Languages at the University of Marburg from 1833 to 1840.

Friedrich August Wolf specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen from circa 1777 to 1779 and served at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1806.

Friedrich Bechtel specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Göttingen, and Strasbourg under Theodor Benfey, August Fick, and others. He worked at Göttingen before becoming a professor of comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg from 1895 until 1923.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1792 to 1796. He held positions at European University Viadrina (circa 1802–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (circa 1811–1848).

Friedrich Bollensen, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University and Main Pedagogical Institute before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Kazan State University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus held professorships across several institutions: the University of Jena (circa 1864–1868), the University of Marburg (circa 1868–1871), the University of Basel (circa 1871–1872), and Kiel University (circa 1872–1888).

Friedrich Carl Andreas was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the temporary chair of Persian at Berlin's Seminar for Oriental Languages and became a professor at Göttingen in 1903.
